assertion_analysis.failure_condition: fails if the discarded run's claim file survives the discard; the base arm and the control-skip mutation both redden it
raises CrewError if the node is still claimed by the discarded run, so a dispatch of the same node is refused
fails if the new dispatch had to displace a stale claim instead of taking a released path
fails if the result omits the released claim path, e.g. if the helper returns nothing
fails if a claim naming another run is unlinked; the control-any mutation reddens it
fails if the other run's claim is gone or has been overwritten, since the dispatch must still be refused naming other-run
compares the claim record to the run id the test itself supplied; it guards the claim mechanism rather than the release, so it cannot redden on a release defect — noted, not a defect in this change

findings.text: The claim is released at :2072 before _remove_discarded_worktree runs at :2073, so a redispatch of the same node can take the freed claim while the discarded run's worktree is still being audited and removed underneath it; evaluating the removal first would close the window, which today only exists because the release is ordered inside the same result literal.
